challenge.notes: No records were extracted. This is a candidate-gene screen of COL4A1 and COL4A2 in Ecuadorian keratoconus families: 48 individuals from 15 families, plus 64 controls. Family KTCN-014 contributed 23 members; 25 affected individuals came from 14 other families. The authors conclude that no causative mutations were found, and that all coding variants are benign or common polymorphisms. They note that Gln1334His (c.4002A>C, rs3742207) in COL4A1 was predicted possibly damaging by PolyPhen but was not significantly associated with disease (p=0.056 within the family; p=0.17 in cases vs controls). The listed missed variants are the coding, UTR, and selected intronic designations printed in the text and Table 2. Table 2 contains many more intronic variants written with en-dash notation; these are also unrecorded. None of these variants is reported as pathogenic.

challenge.notes: This is a population GWAS of retinal vessel traits in UK Biobank (52,798 European-ancestry participants), with replication in EPIC-Norfolk. It contains no proband or family-level COL4A1/COL4A2 variant evidence. The only COL4A1/COL4A2 variant designations are two common intronic/regional SNPs, both associated with arteriolar tortuosity. rs35131825 (COL4A2, p=2.0x10-108) appears in the main text and in Tables C, F and M. rs9559797 (COL4A2, meta-analysis p=6.76e-151) appears in Table E. Table G lists an eQTL at chr13:111054111 affecting COL4A1 and COL4A2 expression, but gives no rs ID. The paper mentions COL4A1 familial retinal arteriolar tortuosity mutations only by citation, with no specific variant designations. If these SNPs are curated at all, they should be treated as GWAS association signals with n_families=0 and no probands, not as pathogenic variants.
